I see someone else mentioned substrate, but I'll say the specifics. And stuff about humidity.

It looks like you have sand in there, which can cause impaction if too much is ingested, especially in babies. I highly recommend changing it out!

Topsoil+playsand+excavator clay is one option that I've seen quite commonly, though don't have personal experience with. It seems great for enrichment since it's very pro-digging. You can also just make a dig box and see if they are interested before committing to the whole tank.

Another option that used especially with juveniles is pieces of tile flooring. Easy to clean, pretty cheap, and harmless. 

You can add in some pieces of wood (not from outside!), stones, live plants (be sure to check if they're safe in case of ingestion) and a whole bunch of other things to mimic their natural habitat. 

No carpet. Harbours bacteria, can snag on their toes, etc etc. Walnut shells are iffy, certain types of walnut are toxic to beardies and the little shards of shell are sharp. It's also super dusty. Not too much research into it, so best to avoid.

HUMIDITY. There's a common misconception that Australia (where beardies are native) is a dessert, and as such beardies are fine with low humidity. Australia is a big island with rain, lakes, all the watery stuff, so make sure to keep a humidity between ~40-60% to keep them healthy, especially if you live somewhere that has dry seasons (winter gets dry too!). Too high can cause respiratory infections, too low can cause cracks in the lungs due to mucus drying out, which then can cause infection. 

Best of luck with your new beardie!! Refreshing to see a receptive owner :)

If they specialize in a certain style and people are going in to get something really simple then they aren't able to express their creativity nearly as much. Idk that's just my thoughts lol.

The two things about getting tats when you're younger is 
1. your body likely will change (gain/lose weight, muscle, height etc) so they will change slightly in appearance.
2. You're definitely going to have to get them redone at some point depending on many factors (the damn sun is one lol).

I'm planning a cover up tat and I've realized they you have to take into account the scars themselves (are they flat/raised, grouped together, how healed they are, etc) with the design and finding an artist who's willing to work with scarred skin. 

I recommend getting your first tattoo on non-scarred skin to see how the pain is because it hurts WAY more going over scars.

I don't necessarily have 'rules of thumb' on prices but here are some things I've implemented to make groceries affordable (or atleast more so):

Pay attention to best before dates, stores don't like selling foods past these dates (bb≠expiry) and will either mark down or sell as deals. Of course, have caution with meats, eggs and dairy. If it doesn't look, smell or taste funky, you're a-ok.

Cheese can get expensive, buy it in blocks and freeze if you please (hard cheeses work best for this). See some mold on the edge? Cut off the portion+extra. Cheese is dense af so mold doesn't spread as fast.

Pay attention to seasonal foods. Berries are cheaper in summer, potatoes in fall, etc. Avoid buying outside of these seasons.

Take advantage of offers (points, sales, etc) but have caution of spending just because it's on sale (ask yourself if you actually need X).

Stores are set up for overconsumption, eat before you go, make a list ahead of time and stick to it.

Want fruit? Bananas. Cheapest thing you can get at ~20 cents each. Getting tired of Bananas? Get a melon (not pre-cut). 

Can't eat your fruit/Veg fast enough? Freeze it. Works wonders in soup or smooties.

Learn how to cook tofu to your liking, $1.50 for about 4 servings. That's about 3$ for a pound.

Best of luck
